name: Buzz cut for thinning hair

card.summary: Clipping hair very short to make thinning or receding hair less noticeable; widely used, with mixed research on how bald and shaved looks are perceived.
card.note: Does not treat hair loss; it changes how it appears.

lead: A buzz cut is a very short hairstyle, clipped to roughly the same length across the head, and is one of the most common ways men manage thinning or receding hair. Wikipedia notes it suits men and boys with thinning or receding hairlines, and can make the face look more defined [1]. Shaving down means moving to a buzz cut or shaved head so the contrast between thinning areas and denser hair, and the line of a receding hairline, becomes less noticeable.

Pattern hair loss affects roughly 30 to 50 percent of men by age 50, and is described as moderately stressful and as reducing body-image satisfaction [2]. A buzz cut changes how the hair looks; it does not treat the underlying condition, for which medical options such as minoxidil, finasteride and hair transplants exist [2]. Many men combine a short cut with those treatments.
The cut is low maintenance and comes in versions from a uniform clip to a fade where the back and sides taper [1].

chain: Less contrast between thinning and denser areas; hairline recession less visible
Head shape and face look more defined, with a clean look
angle.text: Clipping hair to one short length makes thinning crowns and receding temples harder to see. Men use it as a way to look deliberate and tidy without waiting on any treatment.

paras: The buzz cut is also called a wiffle cut and may be clipped uniformly or tapered with a fade. Related styles include the butch cut (one uniform short length on top), the crew cut and the flattop [1]. Wikipedia credits Nikola Bizumic with the manual hair clippers that popularised the cut in the late 19th century, and the style became standard where strict grooming rules applied, including military recruitment in many countries, where it began as a measure against head lice [1].

Wikipedia lists head shaving among ways men manage hair loss, alongside comb-overs and medical treatments [2]. People who shave down generally cite the reduced contrast between sparse and dense areas and the low upkeep [1]. Wikipedia reports that a 2001 South Korean study found most people rated balding men as less attractive, while a 2002 survey of Welsh women rated bald and gray-haired men as quite desirable, and that one theory holds shaved heads signal dominance or high status [2].
No studies found on buzz cuts specifically. Related research on attitudes toward balding and shaved heads is mixed, as described above [2].
Shaving down is a recurring suggestion in hair-loss discussions as an alternative or complement to transplants and drugs. Experiences vary.

timeline.event: Manual hair clippers popularise the buzz cut [1].

lore.intro: Shaving down is a recurring suggestion in hair loss discussions.

claims.claim: A buzz cut hides thinning more effectively than longer hair.
claims.believers: Proponents say uniform short hair reduces visible contrast with the scalp and makes a receding hairline look like a style choice.
claims.experts: No studies were found testing this; Wikipedia notes buzz cuts are popular with people with thinning hair and can make the face look more defined [1].

claims.claim: A shaved head can read as confident or dominant.
claims.experts: Cited research is mixed: a 2001 Korean study rated balding men less attractive, a 2002 Welsh survey rated them desirable [2].
